content:
We now return to study the meaning of the numbers recorded in Numbers chapter ten. We read in Numbers 10:11, "In the second year after Israel's departure from Egypt, on the twentieth day of the second month, the cloud lifted from the Tabernacle of the Covenant." There is rich meaning hidden in this little phrase of time. Over the next few days, we will look at the second year, the second month, and the twentieth day, and we will see what each of them means for the New Creation and what lessons we can learn from them. Today we begin with the second year.

The second year in Numbers ten is not merely a date in Israel's history. It marks a new stage in the journey of God's people. To understand it, we must first look back at the first year. In the first year, Israel experienced redemption. They were brought out of Egypt by the blood of the Passover lamb. They crossed the Red Sea by the mighty power of Yahweh. They came to Mount Sinai and entered into covenant with Him. The first year was the year of deliverance, the year of salvation, the year of separation from Egypt. It was the year they were rescued.

But when we come to the second year, we find that Israel is no longer only a rescued people. They are now a prepared people. During the time at Sinai, Yahweh had given them His Law. The Tabernacle had been built. The cloud of glory had come down and filled it. The priesthood had been established.
The sacrifices had been taught. The tribes had been counted. The camp had been arranged. The Levites had been appointed to their duties. The Passover had been kept a second time. The silver trumpets had been made. Everything was now in order. The people who had simply been rescued in the first year had, by the second year, been shaped and made ready.

So, the second year points us to a new stage that comes after redemption.
It shows us movement after preparation. Israel was not called to remain at Sinai forever. They had been saved out of Egypt, but they were also called to journey forward toward the Promised Land. And notice the order in which Yahweh worked. Before He moved them, He prepared them. Before He sent them forward, He ordered them. Before the cloud lifted, He made them ready. Yahweh never rushed His people out before their time.

This gives us a beautiful lesson for the New Creation. The first stage of our walk with Yahweh is salvation. Just as Israel came out of Egypt, we are delivered from sin, from darkness, from falsehood, and from the world. Through Christ, Yahweh brings us out of our bondage and begins a brand new life within us. This is our first year, our season of deliverance, and it is a season worth rejoicing in. But here is what we must understand; salvation is not the end of the journey. After salvation comes the second stage. God begins to teach us His Word.

He cleanses our thoughts and our desires. He brings order into our life.
He places us within the body of Christ. He shows us our service. He prepares us to walk the narrow way. We are not only rescued from the world; we are being shaped into a holy people for His purpose.

Therefore the second year teaches us that the New Creation must move beyond the joy of simply being delivered. We must also submit ourselves to preparation. We must allow God to build His dwelling in us, to fill us with His Spirit, to teach us His truth, and to arrange our lives according to His will.

Only then can we move forward properly under the leading of the cloud.
Just as Israel did not move until the Tabernacle was established and the cloud lifted, we also must not run ahead by our own strength. We move when Yahweh leads. We serve when He has prepared us. We journey forward when His Word gives the sound. The second year reminds us that after redemption comes preparation, and after preparation comes movement in the purpose of God.

Now there is another beautiful truth connected with this same second year and second month, and it comes to us from the book of Ezra. In Ezra 3:8 we read, "Now in the second year of their coming unto the house of God at Jerusalem,
in the second month, began Zerubbabel and Jeshua to set forward the work of the house of God." This happened after the Jews returned from their long captivity in Babylon. For many years they had been away from their land, away from Jerusalem, and away from the Temple. Their captivity had been the result of their disobedience, yet God did not forget His covenant with them. At the appointed time, He brought His people back from Babylon and gave them the opportunity to rebuild what had been broken down.

But notice the timing very carefully. The rebuilding of the house of God began in the second year and in the second month after they returned. This is a powerful thing when we set it beside Numbers ten. In Numbers ten, Israel moved forward in the second year and the second month after the Tabernacle was established. And in Ezra, the returned captives began rebuilding the Temple in the second year and the second month after returning to Jerusalem. The same pattern of timing appears in both. And so the second year teaches us that after deliverance, there must be restoration. After being brought out of captivity, the work of rebuilding must begin.

This is a great lesson for the New Creation. We were also once in captivity.
We were not held in literal Babylon, but we were in a spiritual bondage just as real; bondage to sin, to wrong teachings, to worldly desires, to fear, to darkness, and to confusion. And the Almighty God, through Christ, has brought us out. He has delivered us from the power of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of His dear Son. But just as with Israel, deliverance is not the end of the work. After He brings us out, He begins to rebuild. For the New Creation is the spiritual house of God. Peter says, "Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house" (1 Peter 2:5). Paul says that we are "builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit" (Ephesians 2:22). Yahweh is not only saving individuals one by one; He is building a spiritual Temple out of them.

Just as Zerubbabel and Jeshua began the work of rebuilding the house of God after the return from Babylon, so Christ is now building the true house of God through the New Creation. He restores what sin destroyed. He rebuilds what false teaching damaged. He repairs what captivity broke. He takes living stones and places them together, forming a dwelling place for Yahweh. And this teaches us that restoration requires order and work. The Jews could not simply return to Jerusalem and sit idle. They had to rise up and build. In the same way, after Yahweh opens our eyes to His truth, we cannot remain passive. We must allow Him to rebuild our minds, our character, our worship, our service, and our fellowship.

So the second year show us a beautiful pattern. After redemption comes preparation. After captivity comes restoration. And after restoration begins the building of Yahweh's house. This is the calling of the New Creation today.

We have been brought out so that we may be built up, and we are being built up so that Yahweh may dwell in us by His Spirit. Let us not only rejoice that we have come out of captivity. Let us also ask ourselves honestly; are we allowing God to rebuild His Temple? Are we being shaped as living stones? Are we helping to build the house of God, or are we delaying the work? Deliverance brings us out, but restoration builds us up. Yahweh did not bring His people out of bondage so that they could remain empty and unfinished.

He brought them out so that His house might be rebuilt, His worship restored, and His glory might dwell among His people once again. Tomorrow, God willing, we will continue with the meaning of the second month.

title: Prayer
text:
O Almighty God,

We thank You that You did not save us only to leave us standing still.

You brought us out of our Egypt, out of our Babylon, out of our bondage;

and now You are building us up as living stones into a dwelling place.

Forgive us for the times we have rejoiced in being delivered yet resisted being rebuilt.

Make us willing to be shaped, ordered, taught, and prepared for Your purpose.

Do not let us delay the work, but let us submit to Your hand as You restore us.

"O give thanks unto Yahweh, for He is good; for His mercy endures forever."

In the name of Christ, the builder of Your house, we pray. Amen.
